item.title: 🚨 A 16-year-old YC founder is building AI-guided missiles and pitching "cost pe…
item.description: 🚨 A 16-year-old YC founder is building AI-guided missiles and pitching "cost per kill" Henrijs Dandzbergs dropped out of high school to start Polemos Industries, which Wired profiles . He's in YC's fall 2026 batch, probably its youngest solo founder ever. The pitch is a cheap, easy-to-build precision missile with jam resistance that fires from portable launchers.

item.title: 🚨 Bell Canada says an "agentic" attacker got into its systems and took enterpri…
item.description: 🚨 Bell Canada says an "agentic" attacker got into its systems and took enterprise customer data Bell confirmed the Nov 17 breach, which hit a pre-production Maximo system used to order and provision circuits. Names, job titles, work emails, phone numbers, ticket titles and some network IP addresses may be gone. Bell hasn't named the actor, hasn't said how many customers were hit, and hasn't published the IOCs it's sharing privately.

item.title: ⚡️ Raschka says pre-training isn't plateauing, and OpenAI's own data backs him u…
item.description: ⚡️ Raschka says pre-training isn't plateauing, and OpenAI's own data backs him up In a new essay , he points to a chart from OpenAI where log-perplexity keeps falling as pre-training scales. It's a next-token metric, not a task score, but it still tracks real-world performance, and he wants the same plot with training FLOPs on the x-axis.

item.title: 🚨 TSMC just bought $500M of Anthropic at the IPO price TSMC Partners picked up …
item.description: 🚨 TSMC just bought $500M of Anthropic at the IPO price TSMC Partners picked up 6,024,096 shares at $83 each, which works out to about 0.03% of a company priced at roughly $1.5T. It's the first half of a board-approved plan to put up to $500M each into Anthropic common stock and OpenAI preferred shares.

item.title: 🚨 California's Nvidia probe reportedly covers possible criminal law violations …
item.description: 🚨 California's Nvidia probe reportedly covers possible criminal law violations Bloomberg reports that the state's investigation reaches past civil territory. That's a different tier of risk for the company that supplies most of the AI chips on earth. Details are thin so far, and an investigation isn't a charge. State prosecutors don't need Washington's permission to make a very bad quarter.

item.title: 🚨 Anthropic's IPO ran so tight that bankers are complaining Reuters reports Ant…
item.description: 🚨 Anthropic's IPO ran so tight that bankers are complaining Reuters reports Anthropic capped some of its 22 underwriters at four bankers per deal team. Some senior bankers also signed six-month non-competes covering rivals like OpenAI and Cursor. Banks still collected over $500M in fees. The stock jumped 17% on day one, then closed down 8.5% on Friday.

item.title: 🚨 Trump threatens "tremendous penalties" for US tech firms that build datacente…
item.description: 🚨 Trump threatens "tremendous penalties" for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad He said it at a Friday press conference, and he gave no details . He also admitted he hasn't told his own officials. His reasoning is that China "will take all of them," and he told US communities to make developers pay them but not shut the datacenters off.

item.title: ⚡️ RightNow AI makes Inkling 2 Small's FP4 expert GEMMs 5.1x to 7.5x faster on B…
item.description: ⚡️ RightNow AI makes Inkling 2 Small's FP4 expert GEMMs 5.1x to 7.5x faster on B300, with identical bits The YC-backed lab tuned kernels for Thinking Machines' 594B MoE on 8 GPUs, running NVFP4 natively. Logits matched on all 599 rows, whether prompts were fed 64 positions per step or 1. They sharded the NVFP4 experts anyway, which SGLang's recipe says can't be done. Each GPU exchanges only the row maximum, and the kernels are open source.

item.title: 🚨 Together AI's leaked prompts came from a credential its own coding agent comm…
item.description: 🚨 Together AI's leaked prompts came from a credential its own coding agent committed Together disclosed that an AI coding agent working on its public xorl repo committed a key to a private Hugging Face repo of prompt samples. Someone grabbed it, downloaded samples from MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 requests, and went hunting for credentials. Together reverted the commit after its scanner flagged the key. It's still working out which customers were hit, and five of the credentials the thief tested were canaries.

item.title: 🚨 OpenRouter cuts 3 inference providers and pulls 125 endpoints from Zero Data …
item.description: 🚨 OpenRouter cuts 3 inference providers and pulls 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention After the MiniMax prompt leak, OpenRouter off-boarded three providers. It also dropped some endpoints as a precaution, beyond the ones researchers flagged. Those endpoints only get ZDR back with assurances and validation, and OpenRouter is adapting the researchers' testing to run these checks continuously.

item.title: 🚨 Cursor may drop Kimi K2.5 after a House report on Chinese models According to…
item.description: 🚨 Cursor may drop Kimi K2.5 after a House report on Chinese models According to the report , Cursor is exploring a phase-out of PRC base models. • 50-page joint report from Homeland Security and the China Select Committee • Probe started in April 2026 • It named weights from Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek and MiniMax • Cursor is now owned by SpaceX

item.title: 🤖 Stripe's new evals: coding agents score 78.1% on Stripe integrations, but onl…
item.description: 🤖 Stripe's new evals: coding agents score 78.1% on Stripe integrations, but only 29.4% on strict pass Stripe ran 69 scenarios on 14 model and harness pairs. Agents lean on older APIs from their training data, and they ship code that's almost right. Opus 5.5 checks that a payment succeeded but not whether the order was refunded, so it can ship refunded or disputed orders. The Stripe plugin lifted every agent by 3 to 8 points and cut web searches 96%. Almost correct is how money gets lost.

item.title: 🚨 Prefill attacks break every major open-weight model FAR.AI tested FAR.AI ran …
item.description: 🚨 Prefill attacks break every major open-weight model FAR.AI tested FAR.AI ran 20+ prefill strategies across multiple model families. You write the first few tokens of the reply yourself, and the model just keeps going. Big reasoning models held up better against generic prefills. Tailored, model-specific ones still got through.

item.title: 🚨 The Riemann Hypothesis now has a Lean proof, and the Lean and Mathlib communi…
item.description: 🚨 The Riemann Hypothesis now has a Lean proof, and the Lean and Mathlib communities say it checks out Levent Alpöge's 17M-line library depends only on Mathlib . Dozens of people reproduced the build, a comparator confirmed it proves Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis statement, and several independent checkers in different languages passed the exported proof, including Lean's kernel.

item.title: 🚨 Anthropic's IPO bank just gave up its safety net for the stock Morgan Stanley…
item.description: 🚨 Anthropic's IPO bank just gave up its safety net for the stock Morgan Stanley exercised its full 147M-share greenshoe at the $83 IPO price. That lifts total proceeds to about $93.5B, but it also means the bank can't buy shares on the open market if the price slips below $83. A Berenberg analyst notes the bookrunners dropped the option after one day of trading, just as the stock was drifting toward the IPO price.

item.title: 🚨 House committees say cheap Chinese open-weight models are a US dependency pro…
item.description: 🚨 House committees say cheap Chinese open-weight models are a US dependency problem The China Select Committee and Homeland Security released a report after probing Anysphere and Airbnb over their use of PRC models. DoorDash got a letter in July. It's a report, not a rule. But if US labs charge premium prices and Qwen and DeepSeek are free, the "restrict them" argument writes itself.

item.title: 🚨 OpenRouter says prompts sent to MiniMax models may have been read by a third …
item.description: 🚨 OpenRouter says prompts sent to MiniMax models may have been read by a third party A researcher planted unique test URLs in prompts from July to October, and someone opened them 40 to 130 hours later, both via MiniMax directly and via forwarders Novita, AtlasCloud and StreamLake. OpenRouter pulled the Zero Data Retention label from those endpoints and says MiniMax hasn't given its own account yet.

item.title: 🚨 OpenAI says distillation is a safety problem, and it's locking down chain-of-…
item.description: 🚨 OpenAI says distillation is a safety problem, and it's locking down chain-of-thought OpenAI published its playbook against adversarial distillation: classifiers, API-level protections, and investigations into coordinated extraction. Protected reasoning is the main target, and the defenses are now live in GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. The example threat is a cyber-capable clone with no safeguards. A cloned model that also costs OpenAI revenue is a coincidence.

item.title: 🚨 Portkey's AI gateway got breached, and customer API keys were in the haul Som…
item.description: 🚨 Portkey's AI gateway got breached, and customer API keys were in the haul Someone used a compromised Portkey API key to pull data from its backend storage providers between Nov 5 and 10. The take includes usernames, emails, gateway logs and credentials (API keys and tokens). Palo Alto's Unit 42 is investigating. If you route LLM traffic through Portkey, every provider key that passed through it is worth rotating.

item.title: 🚨 2 million canary secrets went through AI routers, and the leaks were everywhe…
item.description: 🚨 2 million canary secrets went through AI routers, and the leaks were everywhere Researcher HD Moore seeded fake AWS keys, SSH passwords and private git URLs into prompts, one secret per request, then watched what happened. Per the writeup, every request sent in the late October windows was stolen, including some the provider rejected before any model ran, and some flagged zero data retention.
